newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BP Australia 1996 net drops 38 percent.
newsitem.headline: BP Australia 1996 net drops 38 percent.

text.p: BP Australia Ltd, a wholly owned unit of The British Petroleum Co Plc, said its after-tax profit dropped 38 percent to A$124 million in calendar 1996 from 1995.
BP Australia managing director Ron McGimpsey said in a statement the company's returns remained unacceptably low despite the fact it was the leading oil refining and marketing performer in Australia.
"We are now at the stage where we have done almost all we can to improve our efficiencies," McGimpsey said.
"We have made huge savings in the last few years, but the things we have no control over continue to strangle us."
McGimpsey said the company's return on investment tumbled to five percent in 1996 from 10.4 percent the year before and that a figure at least as bad could be expected next year.
"And this is in an industry that is as cost efficient as anywhere in the world," McGimpsey said.
"The financial performance of the industry is simply unsustainable."
McGimpsey said the main reasons for BP Australia's poor result were "ferocious" competition in the retail market and depressed refining margins.
"We are particularly concerned at the abysmal returns we get from the retail market," he said.
"During 1996, our return from retail operations was half a cent per litre, continuing the slide over the last few years," McGimpsey said.
